claims.claim: smACG constructs can generate adenine-, cytosine-, and guanine-associated conversions within the same allele.
smACGmax reached up to 41 percent simultaneous triple-base conversion in tested sequence contexts.
In the 71 HBEGF sites described in the rebuttal, triple-conversion alleles ranged from 0.3 to 28 percent with a mean of 5.5 percent.
Guanine editing retains an NGR-context preference and average efficiency near 20 percent in the discussed comparisons.
The HBEGF screen achieved 94 percent targeted mutagenesis coverage and identified diphtheria-toxin-resistant variants.
smACGmax was the first triple-base editor.
smACGmax provides universal or saturated access to all possible local substitutions.
A valid pre-intervention biological phase variable was measured for each edited cell or matched population.
A specific enriched triple-edited allele caused diphtheria-toxin resistance.

rules: Do not substitute the maximum triple-editing rate for a typical or across-target rate.
Do not treat selected-population enrichment as direct causal proof for a specific allele without linkage evidence.
Do not restore a priority claim removed during peer review.
Do not infer a Kairos phase variable from collection time alone.
